review.assessment:
The change introduces a new `median()` function in `cohort/stats.py` that computes the middle index using integer division (`n // 2`). This logic bypasses the requirement to average the two central values when the dataset contains an even number of elements, directly contradicting the finance standard where [3000, 4200, 4400, 5000] must yield 4300. As written, any report feeding even-length cohorts into this function will produce systematically incorrect medians.

Defects found:
1. **Even-length median ignores averaging**
   - `call`: `python -c "from cohort.stats import median; print(median([3000, 4200, 4400, 5000]))"`
   - `expected`: 4300
   - `actual`: 4400
